questions.q: What does the `stg_` prefix promise about a model, according to this lesson?
options: That it's 1-to-1 with a source table, renamed and typed, with no joins or aggregations
That it is materialized as an incremental table
That it contains business-defined, denormalized data
That it can safely be queried directly by a BI tool
questions.explain: stg_ signals the staging-layer contract: 1-to-1 with a source, renamed and typed, no joins or aggregations.

questions.q: Why does this lesson present fct_/dim_ as a real but not universal convention?
options: dbt Labs' main marts guidance leads with plain entity nouns, but dbt Labs' own exposures example uses fct_orders and dim_customers, so both are real, sourced conventions
fct_/dim_ is a Power BI convention that has nothing to do with dbt
dbt Labs has deprecated fct_/dim_ entirely and it should never be used
fct_/dim_ only applies to staging models, never marts
questions.explain: Both plain nouns and fct_/dim_ are real dbt Labs-sourced conventions — the lesson presents them honestly rather than picking one as the only correct answer.

questions.q: Who or what actually enforces dbt naming conventions like stg_ and int_?
options: Team habit and code review — dbt itself does not enforce or require any particular naming prefix
The dbt CLI, which refuses to run a model with the wrong prefix
The data warehouse, which rejects incorrectly named tables
The dbt_project.yml file, which auto-renames models on save
questions.explain: dbt would happily run a staging model named 'final_report_v2' — nothing in the tool enforces naming. The convention is a team discipline.

questions.q: Why does naming consistency matter more as a project scales from six models to sixty?
options: A reviewer needs to gauge a change's layer and risk from a filename alone, and searches like `git grep stg_` need to return exactly the right set of models
dbt runs slower with inconsistent names at scale
Warehouses charge extra for inconsistently named tables
It doesn't matter more — naming conventions only matter for small projects
questions.explain: At scale, nobody holds the whole project in their head — the filename has to carry the information a person used to just remember.

questions.q: What is the real cost of 'naming drift' in a dbt project, according to this lesson?
options: The DAG still technically works, but every new person has to re-learn, model by model, what's actually going on because names stopped telling the truth
dbt refuses to compile the project until names are fixed
All existing tests automatically fail
The lineage graph stops rendering entirely
questions.explain: dbt doesn't care what you name things — the cost of drift is entirely human: lost trust and repeated re-learning, not a technical failure.
